Here is a shameless plug for my project. It is a esp32 based programmable keyboard (HID) with a web interface and api. It can be directly flashed to the m5stack atom or m5stack cardputer.

One stand-out feature it has is an implementation of the Keepass KDBX database standard. The database can be stored on FRAM or SD card and can be unlocked via the web interface. The key is stored in volatile memory. There is a DSL scripting language that can be used to run macros, programs, or functions. With the database unlocked you can send credentials via key-value DSL strings such as the following example: {credstore myusername} {TAB} {credstore mypassword} {ENTER}

evan_a_a · Nov 7, 2026

BLE is not insecure if you configure the pairing process to use LE Secure Connections with authenticated pairing, which does exactly what you have implemented (ECDH key agreement). "Just Works" pairing is the only method vulnerable to MITM because it doesn't require out-of-band confirmation.

SV_BubbleTime · Nov 7, 2026

Further, “just works” Bluetooth encryption is not vulnerable most of the time. It’s only vulnerable at the instance of pairing.

It shares exchanges a pre-shared key one time at pairing then trusts that both sides will remember the PSK.

So long as you pair while there is definitely nobody around and sniffing Bluetooth traffic, it’s an excellent system.

But the author clearly wanted to go through the effort of implementing Duffy Hellman for this.
